Why does your brain think 3.99 is three dollars?
A shopkeeper prices a lamp at four dollars, and sells none.
So he drops it one cent, to 3.99, and sells a pile.
One cent. That is the trick.
Turns out, your brain reads a price left to right, and mostly stops at the first digit.
Four dollars looks like a four. Three ninety-nine looks like a three.
So your brain rounds it down, and the cheaper-feeling number wins.
Studies find that prices just under a round number tend to sell more than one cent should explain.
But the lamp is still worth about four dollars.
So read the left digit, then ask what it is really worth.
The shopkeeper knows. He still sells lamps at 3.99.
